quest.title: A Wangshan Walk to Remember
quest.description: At Huang the Third's invitation, you arrive at the legendary place where the treasure of the Guhua Clan is located, Wangshan Hall...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x35000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Excuse me... What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: Wangshan Hall.

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: If you're lost... keep following that road over there, it'll take you to Yilong Wharf.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Wangshan Hall? Now where has Paimon heard this name before...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah! Paimon remembers now! ... That's the stronghold of the Guhua Clan, right!?

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: ...Indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Paimon never expected it would be in this sort of place... Well, can we go in and look around?

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: Look around, you say? I didn't think outsiders would want to visit such a remote, mountainous place!

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: But since you're here, let me fetch one of my seniors to show you around. I'm not urbane or eloquent enough to receive visitors, I fear.

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: You two wait here while I go to Yilong Wharf. I won't be long!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Even before the voice of Wen the Fourth has faded, he has turned and disappeared into the forest...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Impressive! Now you see him, now you don't!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So that's real qinggong in action, eh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, hang on a second. Did he just say Yilong Wharf!? So how long are we gonna be waiting!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, seeing as he's proficient in martial arts, it probably won't take him too long to get from here to there...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nothing for it but to wait, then.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: It is not long before Wen the Fourth returns with another person...

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Hey, c'mon, a bit slower, will you? These old bones can't keep up with your pace...

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: ...I AM going slow. And let's be real, you're the one who's neglected your skills for so long that you've put on all this meat...

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Enough, that's enough. Don't say such things in front of visitors!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Er, and this old gentleman is...?

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Huang the Third of the Guhua Clan. Some people know me as the Cloudpiercing Arrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cloudpiercing Arrow...? So you're a talented archer?

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Haha, it was just a moniker bestowed on me in my youth. Pay it no mind.

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: Hmph, what do you mean "bestowed upon"? You just call yourself that...

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Why don't you just keep a lid on it? Ahem... Anyway, you'd like to visit Wangshan Hall, right?

choices.text: That's right.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Haha, very good! With your skills, perhaps you might find the treasures left by Grand Master Guhua!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Treasures!?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Quite so! Grand Master Guhua secretly established 12 Secret Chambers within the Hall upon the Clan's founding, in which he placed treasures now lost to the world.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: 12 Secret Chambers, eh? That's very specific of you. Did you take the time to count them yourself...?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Tsk...

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Whatever. Go on, go on.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Wangshan Hall is hewn from the mountain stone itself, and its structure is complex and intricate. Over millennia, only a handful of these hidden chambers have been discovered. The locations of many others are unknown even to us disciples.

choices.text: (This has to be a gimmick to sucker tourists in...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #For real!? {NICKNAME}, {NICKNAME}! Let's go see those secret Guhua Clan treasures, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what's with that look? Aren't you tempted at all? We'll be rich if we find that forgotten treasure!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Fine then. Lead the way, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, awesome! Paimon just knew that you'd be interested!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hang on, how much does it cost to tour Wangshan Hall?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Cost? Haha, surely you jest! We are honorable disciples of the Guhua Clan, and wish only to invite those of character to come visit. We are not brash, swindling charlatans!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: I'm not even asking for a penny! How about it? Would you care to come with me for a tour, and together explore our clan's illustrious history?

choices.text: Great, that's just what I was thinking!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Haha, you certainly are direct!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: However, Wangshan Hall is, in the end, very important to us. Custom dictates, therefore, that outsiders who wish to enter must first pass two trials.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Put another way, we first wish to see just how skilled you are!

choices.text: Hmph, don't underestimate us!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Of course, of course! These two tests will certainly be a walk in the park for your illustrious selves!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: It's just that these are the rules of our clan, and we can't simply change them arbitrarily. Please forgive me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, what exactly do I need to do?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: It's very simple. Please, follow me!

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Stay safe, you two.

choices.text: This is so troublesome...

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Brother, you... Calm yourself. Stop interrupting me!

response.speaker: Huang the Third

Therefore, prithee tarry a while, as I make so bold to request your good name?

choices.text: Not bad. You've got good eyes for some old guy!

response.speaker: Paimon

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a minute, did you just say... Guhua Clan?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Oh? Are you familiar with our clan's name?

choices.text: It rings a bell.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Excellent, excellent! I thought the Clan's fortunes had waned so much that its name was now all but forgotten. I did not expect you to be so well-informed.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: To be frank, I approached you because I am inviting select interested parties to visit Wangshan Hall, our Clan stronghold, and explore history itself.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: If you have nowhere pressing to be, how about coming with me to see the Hall? I promise you won't be disappointed!

choices.text: You're turning your stronghold into a tourist attraction?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Err... Well, our disciples are scattered all over Liyue. As the Hall is currently deserted, what better time to invite guests?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: What's more, it contains treasures never before seen...

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Behold the Plumwatcher Piles, passed down by Grand Master Guhua!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: It was upon these stones that Grand Master Guhua practiced back in the day, diligently cultivating the technique to become a true master! Over there, the ancient trees were also planted by our founder's hand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, they're all at crazy angles, and some are even broken in half...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's probably due to years of disrepair and neglect...

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Ahem... Of course not! It's merely to increase the difficulty of the training, nothing more! After all, there won't be neat stone piles to step on in a real battle, will there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nobody would step on one of these things in a real fight either!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: #...In any case! For the first trial, I ask that you step on the stone piles in the order I specify within the allotted time, {NICKNAME}. Show me what you've got!

choices.text: Heh, piece of cake!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: #Alright then. You're up, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: This is so troublesome...

dialogues.text: Such extraordinary technique! You moved like a swallow in flight, with not a droplet of water staining your wings. Such unparalleled grace is truly worthy of a hero!

choices.text: Heh, it was nothing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Does using a wind glider count as a technique?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Haha, it looks like you still have much to learn about traditional martial arts, child.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: I ask you this: When a wandering hero strides out and brings bandits and thieves alike to justice, was it their skill that deserves credit, or their sword's?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... The hero's skill, of course!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Correct! Even the sharpest blade is ineffective in the hands of one who knows not how to wield it.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: #It is by this same reasoning that {NICKNAME} could use {M#his}{F#her} wind glider so superbly. This is the kind of mastery we strive for in Guhua martial arts!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: #With that, let me congratulate you on acing the first trial, {NICKNAME}! For the second trial, we must proceed to the practice arena. Please come with me!

response.speaker: Player

choices.text: I almost fell...

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Behold, our practice arena!

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Back then, the reputation of the Guhua Clan was known throughout Liyue. But what was it based on? It was based on the spear and sword skills developed right here!

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: The dual mastery of polearm and sword we are known for is the result of arduous practice, day after day!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's nobody here...)

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: This is the second trial, the Trial of Spear and Sword! Just one moment while I get the training equipment out...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Huang the Third produces a bunch of dusty bamboo dummies from somewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Phew, I'm exhausted... Okay! Anyway, would you please display your skills on these dummies?

choices.text: Sure, but what exactly should I do?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Take a look. Some of these dummies are <color=#80CCFFFF>dressed in blue</color> while others are <color=#FF8080FF>dressed in red</color>.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: The battlefield may turn on a dime. You must be able to distinguish friend from foe. To clear this trial, defeat all the dummies <color=#FF8080FF>dressed in red</color> within the allotted time!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: #If you strike a dummy <color=#80CCFFFF>dressed in blue</color>, you lose. Stay alert, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon gets it! So, you have to attack the dummies <color=#FF8080FF>in red</color> without hitting a single dummy <color=#80CCFFFF>in blue</color>...

choices.text: Pff, simple. Behold my power!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Great! That's the spirit! In this case, let's get started!

choices.text: Can you repeat that, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Let's see... Paimon thinks he's saying you can only hit... the ones <color=#FF8080FF>in blue</color>, right? But you can't hit any of the ones <color=#80CCFFFF>in red</color>...

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: You've got it the wrong way around! You must attack all the dummies <color=#FF8080FF>dressed in red</color> without hitting a single one that's <color=#80CCFFFF>dressed in blue</color>!

choices.text: Could you say that one more time?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Eh? It's... You have to hit all those dressed in... Ahem, anyway, you get the idea!

choices.text: Oh, I see! The second trial is a tongue twister...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It really isn't! Even though Paimon's a little confused... At least, just hit all the dummies of one color, which is... red? Probably...

choices.text: Surely you don't expect me to knock all these dummies down in two seconds flat or something...?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Haha, surely you jest! Who could train in such a ludicrous fashion?

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: I'm not sure what delicacy you've prepared, but I'll just wait over here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woohoo! That means we've successfully cleared the stage, right?

choices.text: It was a piece of cake!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: A—Amazing! You effortlessly defeated all the targets with outstanding speed and accuracy! Even among our disciples, few can ever hope to rival you!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Are you the master of another clan, here on some secret visit?

choices.text: Indeed. I'm, in truth, the master of the Paimon Clan...

response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: #The dummies in red that {NICKNAME} just spared were our undercover agents! Hitting them by accident would be no different from hitting ourselves on the head!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: U—Undercover agents? How could you tell?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Haha! Don't you understand, little one? As they say, you never know what lurks on the inside. How could they be distinguished by appearance alone?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: #Yet, {NICKNAME} saw through their appearance and peered into their very nature! Such perception truly is the pinnacle of skill!

choices.text: Exactly!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait! Just wait! Dummies don't have a nature! And you, {NICKNAME}! Stop looking so smug! You just failed to finish them off, right?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Anyway, as you've passed two trials, you've naturally earned the right to visit Wangshan Hall. Please come with me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's a pass? Well... As long as it gets us in... Look out, Treasures of Guhua, 'cause here we come!

choices.text: Are you even listening to yourself right now...
It's all because this platform is too dang slippery!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Why are you just standing there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There goes the stage, and the treasure with it...

choices.text: I lost concentration for a sec, that's all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Paimon didn't know you could zone out even at a time like this...

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Excellent! I've never met someone so understanding and righteous in all my life! I truly admire you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait! There's nothing to admire about that! {NICKNAME} just stood there on the spot!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Haha! You fail to see beyond the surface of things!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s skill is more than enough to instantly take down all those dummies in red. But that is not the Way.

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Some swords in this world take life, and some give it. Taking life is easy, and giving it, hard. And the greatest principle in martial arts is to not kill!

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: #While they may be dummies made of bamboo, they still symbolize living beings. {NICKNAME}'s compassion and decision to feign distraction just to protect the innocent, even at the cost of failing the trial... It's truly admirable!

choices.text: Heh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What the heck is this nonsense... Hey, {NICKNAME}! Stop looking so smug! You were just distracted, weren't you!?

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Anyway, as you've passed two trials, you've naturally earned the right to visit Wangshan Hall. Please come with me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's a pass? Well... As long as it gets us in... Look out, Treasures of Guhua, 'cause here we come!

choices.text: Well, I really was distracted...

response.speaker: Huang the Third
response.text: Haha! There's no need for humility! I'm fully capable of distinguishing your true intent!

choices.text: Huh? What did you just say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Stop messing with Paimon!

choices.text: I have no idea which ones I'm supposed to hit...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Well, you do have a point... How are we supposed to know which ones to hit between all the dummies of different colors...

choices.text: Tell me about the trials...

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Outsiders who seek to enter Wangshan Hall must pass two trials. This rule has existed since ancient times.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: However... Forget it, if my senior thinks it's all right, then I have nothing to say about it. Anyway, there's nothing to worry about. <color=#00E1FFFF>Anyone can pass</color> the trials as they are right now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh? What do you mean?

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: ...You will understand soon enough. Go on, don't let me keep you. My senior is waiting.

choices.text: We'll be on our way then. Goodbye!

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Go on, my senior is waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: ...Skilled.

choices.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: I said you're skilled.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: But you need more practice if you seek to further yourself.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: I saw the way you moved just now. I won't comment on the details, but it was pretty good overall. I'm certain it will become a great weapon in your arsenal if you work hard on it.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Hah... I may say that, but even now, it far surpasses anything my senior is capable of.

choices.text: Thanks for the compliment.
You seem hesitant to say something...

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Forget it... If my senior thinks it's all right, then I have nothing to say about it. So don't ask me.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: I never expected our clan to end up in such a state... Yet there is nothing that can be done...

choices.text: Hey! So what do you think about my skill!?

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: If you have anything to ask about the Guhua Clan... Feel free to ask me. As for what my senior said... Don't believe everything he says.

choices.text: Tell me about Wangshan Hall...

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Wangshan Hall is the main house of the Guhua Clan and where Grand Master Guhua attained enlightenment.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Now, it is in ruins and unusable... Besides my senior and I, no one else remains to guard this place.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Even our current Master merely visits occasionally.

choices.text: So, what's the clan's history...

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: The Guhua Clan was once known as the Guhua Brotherhood. We looked up to the chivalry of Grand Master Guhua and traveled the world with our swords and spears... Our mastery of both was known to all.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Sigh... But as time passed, the clan's glory was no more...

choices.text: Mastery over spear and sword?

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Exactly. The Guhua Clan has three ultimate techniques — Light Piercer, Rain Cutter, and Life Ender. The three were known as the Three Guhua Greats.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Life Ender is a unique fusion of sword and spear, and it is why the Guhua Clan is known to have mastery over both.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: It is said that Life Ender could slice wind, split waves, and destroy mountains. Unfortunately, I never had the chance to witness it for myself.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Later on, during the time of the 11th Master... Yingmin, the one known as the Piercing Blade, felt that these techniques were too difficult to master and unsuitable for widespread study. Slight modifications were made to develop a new set of entry-level techniques...

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: And the outcome of that was... Few were willing to give up the easily attainable for hard work, and fewer and fewer were willing to meditate and spend decades on the original teachings of Grand Master Guhua...

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: As time flashed by, our three ultimate techniques gradually became legendary, yet their power was ever-weakening. Our clan's vigor wound up declining and faith in it was lost... A shame. A shame, indeed...

choices.text: I see...
Tell me about the Guhua Clan...

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Grand Master Guhua was our founder, but not the clan's first master.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: The grand master was a wandering hero who brought peace and justice to the people while traveling the world. He never intended to start a clan. This place wasn't always known as Wangshan Hall, instead being known as the "Lingmeng Chamber."

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: After the grand master passed away, Boxuan... better known as Master Baixuan, who once received his favor, established the Guhua Brotherhood in his name and called himself a disciple of Guhua to carry on the grand master's legacy.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So they were a self-proclaimed disciple?

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Indeed. The grand master never took one.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Unfortunately, the glory of the clan faded with time. We, disciples of future generations, failed the clan. Now, we no longer seek to restore the clan's glory, merely to uphold justice and live up to the grand master's name.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And that's why the disciples of the Guhua Clan are spread all over Liyue?

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: Exactly. After all, there are places in the world where the sun doesn't shine, and we cannot leave everything to Rex Lapis.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: But... My only consolation is a promising junior — Xingqiu. If he can restore our former glory... Then we of the older generation can die without regrets.

choices.text: I want to take a look at Wangshan Hall.

response.speaker: Wen the Fourth
response.text: ...Forgive me for not accompanying you. Farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: Sigh... To think that after a thousand years of heritage, the Guhua Clan's head doorkeeper must cheat others to survive... What shall we do, what can be done...

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Ugh... Alright, come on now. Am I not sparing my junior from starving to death while guarding our gates...?

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: #And don't look at me like that. You're always depressed... But you were pleased to see {NICKNAME}'s performance just now, weren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: That fool from before? They get to take a look around in exchange for making you a meal? And I should be pleased about that? Were I a few years younger, I would slay you in one smack...

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Heh! Your technique was inferior to mine just a few years ago!

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: ...Anyway, listen... Only a few of us geezers are left. What do you plan to do after we stop testing those who may be destined to join us? Take those books with us to our graves?

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Hah... Just forget it. What's the point of saying such depressing things?

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Oh, why don't you try the food those kids made me? Hehe! I think it's better than Wanmin Restaurant's fare! Here, take a bite! Just a bite!

dialogues.speaker: Wen the Fourth
dialogues.text: (No... How can you take those antiques out without maintaining them!? What if...)

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: (Hey, you don't get it... If I did that, and people saw that the paint was new, would they still be willing to come play... I mean, come train!? The sense of history is... whatchamacallit... Hey!)

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: (...And anyway, the two of us don't have that much spare cash...)

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Simply incredible! This way next, please.

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: #Not bad! Your skill is truly extraordinary, {M#Young Hero}{F#Young Heroine}!

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Okay! Almost there, one last step!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}, what are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: #Not bad, that's exactly it! You truly are wise and farsighted beyond ordinary folk, {M#Young Hero}{F#Young Heroine}, and you have superb skill, too!

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Behold! This is the arsenal of Wangshan Hall! Spears, swords, halberds... Anything you can think of, you'll find it here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anything and everything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? There seems to be a censer here.

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Haha, good eye! The memorial tablet of our ancestral founder, Guhua, is enshrined here!

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Our grand master traveled the world, and the only reason the clan has lasted a thousand years is because the world admires his virtue and remembers him with gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, Huang the Third... The way you're walking...

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Haha! How embarrassing! Anyway, this is the Guhua Clan's secret movement technique — Soaring Swallow! Forgive me for not showing it to you earlier, but it's a rule of our clan...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, Paimon just wanted to ask... You're shaking like a leaf all of a sudden. Are you not feeling well? Or do you just need a break...

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: This tablet is here to remind future generations of our clan to never forget the teachings of our ancestors... To help those in need and bring peace to the people.

dialogues.speaker: Huang the Third
dialogues.text: Ah. As ever, this is such a wondrous sight! Although only a few shields and spears remain, I'm sure the grand scenes of the past are already flashing before your eyes!
